newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong, Thailand sign air services agreement.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong, Thailand sign air services agreement.

text.p: Hong Kong and Thailand signed an air services agreement on Monday, the Hong Kong government said.
The agreement is the 18th signed by Hong Kong and will straddle the British territory's handover to China on July 1.

Economic Services Secretary Stephen Ip said in a statement the Thai market was important to Hong Kong flagship carrier Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, which operates 35 flights a week to Bangkok, as well as Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair), which flies three times a week to Phuket.
The two airlines carried a total of some 900,000 passengers to Thailand last year, the statement said.
Thai Airways International Plc operates 46 flights per week to the territory and carried 1.04 million passengers in 1996, it said.

Hong Kong also has accords with the Netherlands, Switzerland, Canada, Brunei, France, New Zealand, Malaysia, Brazil, Sri Lanka, Australia, Germany, South Korea, Singapore, Italy, India, Japan and Burma.
